Home
A warm welcome from Mrs Liz Thomas-Friend (Executive Headteacher)
In September 2016 I was delighted to be appointed as Executive Headteacher at St Alphege. I work as Executive Headteacher of both St Alphege CE Infant School and Herne CE Infant School. I am very fortunate that in both schools there is a strong Head of School who leads the schools on a day to day basis.
I trained as an Early Years Specialist and have taught the infant age range in a variety of schools across the country. I have had the opportunity to work with amazing practitioners and have an interest in the international dimension of education, visiting Finland, Sweden and Canada to explore education systems.
I believe that every child should be valued, respected and loved and that well-being and involvement is paramount to the success of each child’s life chances. I recognise the importance of the home-school relationship and that by working together we enable your children to achieve. The Arts and curriculum enrichment has such a vital role in children’s lives and as practitioners and parents we must ensure that our children receive the very best provision.
I am very excited that my role will harness the strengths of both schools so that the school communities can access outstanding learning environments and share their expertise with each other.
The opportunity to share the Celebration of Childhood across Herne Bay and Whitstable is a real privilege and I look forward to ensuring that your children experience a love of learning which will last a lifetime.
Liz Thomas-Friend, Executive Head
A warm welcome from Mrs Jacqui Spinks (Head of School)
Early Years and Infant education is my passion and is where I have spent the majority of my career. I believe that if we can inspire a love for learning in children from the start, this will have a dramatic impact on the way they see themselves as learners in the future. At St Alphege we strive to create an irresistible curriculum that inspires our children and provides them with rich and purposeful learning opportunities.
Music and the Arts is another passion of mine and I am incredibly proud to have secured Arts Mark Platinum status for the school in September 2019. I have previously worked as a Leading Music teacher supporting schools across the Canterbury district to improve or maintain their Music provision. I believe that the Arts are an essential element of education as they equip children with the skills to be creative, confident and excellent communicators. They learn to solve problems, persevere and work in collaboration with others. Participating in Music, Drama and Art opportunities gives children the tools for living life reflectively, joyfully and with the ability to shape the future.
I started my career at St Alphege as an Inclusion Leader and Deputy Headteacher and have worked for many years supporting pupils with Special Educational Needs. I am very committed to inclusive education, creating a school environment where well-being is high on the agenda and supporting all pupils regardless of their backgrounds or starting points.
St Alphege CE Infant School and Sunbeams Nursery is a truly wonderful place to be and I am incredibly proud to be the Head of School. Our position in the centre of vibrant Whitstable enables excellent community links and exciting learning opportunities outside of the school. The staff team are committed and share my passion to provide the very best for the children in our care. I look forward to ensuring that your children achieve our school motto of “Learning to Live and Loving to Learn” in an environment where the children will always come first.
Jacqui Spinks, Head of School

pageCache.pageTitle: St Alphege CE Infant School - Outstanding Music Provision
pageCache.text:
Outstanding Music Provision
We are delighted to have been awarded with our Music Mark for another year. This is awarded by Kent Music School in recognition of outstanding music provision. We have been commended for our rich, exciting, high-quality and engaging music curriculum and the additional musical experiences we provide for all children. The Music Mark celebrates schools that also influence others in understanding the important contribution that music makes in every school and makes established relationships with professionals within the music sector and the wider community of music educators.
St Alphege is proud to offer an exceptional music curriculum for all children, delivered by highly specialist teaching staff. We also use music as a vehicle to drive other subjects for example, you will see composition used to support storytelling and singing used in all parts of the curriculum. We offer a range of tuition in both groups and individually, so your child will have many opportunities to begin their journey into learning an instrument. The school also has a strong choir and teaches ukulele, ocarina and djembe drumming to all children during their time at the school.
We are honoured to have been invited to join the Kent and Medway Lead Schools Advisory Group for music. Kent Music work closely with schools, colleges, cultural organisations and other partners to ensure that children and young people across Kent and Medway have access to high quality music education in and out of school. We are delighted to have been successful in being asked to join the Lead Schools Advisory Group, which has been set up to support the Hub’s strategic thinking and approach to supporting music making activities in schools across Kent and Medway. This is a wonderful opportunity and a huge achievement for the school. It is a further acknowledgement of our strength, commitment and passion for Music and Creativity. We are looking forward to working alongside the Hub to help shape the vision for the Lead Schools Advisory Group and hope to be able to inspire other schools to embrace a rich and inspiring Music offer for young people across Kent and Medway. We are the first primary school in the South East to have joined the group and are excited about being a part of this new venture alongside the music hub.
To find out more about Kent Music and what they have to offer, please click on the link below:
https://www.kent-music.com/
Due to our recognised strengths in all aspects of the Arts, we were asked to write a blog for Kent Music School outlining our outstanding practice. You can read the blog on the link below:
Kent Music School wrote: "St Alphege CE Infant School and Sunbeams Nursery stands as a beacon of creativity and artistic excellence. This remarkable institution has not only achieved Artsmark Platinum status but also proudly bears the Music Mark school recognition, setting a precedent for arts and music education. We spoke to Jacqui Spinks, the Head of School, to delve into her journey of creating a musical universe through a primary arts focus."
https://schools.kent-music.com/home/services-for-schools/kent-music-schools-blog/primary-arts-music-mark-artsmark/

pageCache.pageTitle: St Alphege CE Infant School - Artsmark Platinum
pageCache.text:
Artsmark Platinum
Our School»
Artsmark Platinum»
St Alphege CE Infant School in Whitstable becomes the first Infant School in the South East to achieve Platinum Artsmark Status!
St Alphege has received and retained the prestigious Platinum Artsmark Award since 2019. This is highest level awarded by Arts Council England and follows a rigorous application process. To achieve Platinum level Artsmark, St Alphege had to demonstrate embedded and exciting arts in the curriculum, extracurricular activities, working with artists and arts organisations, arts outreach work with other schools and organisations and evaluating the impact of the arts on the whole community.
This is even more significant as our children are all under the age of seven years old. Through our child centred approach and belief in the potential for each individual, we allow our children’s curiosity and imagination to have no limits.
“Before a child talks, they sing. Before they write, they draw. As soon as they stand, they dance. Art is fundamental to human expression.” P. Rashad
We were assessed against seven Quality Principles:
1. Striving for excellence and innovation
3. Being exciting, inspiring and engaging
4. Ensuring a positive and inclusive experience
5. Actively involving children and young people
6. Enabling personal progression
7. Developing belonging and ownership
Children as young as 4 years old, have the opportunity to develop leadership skills within the arts, working both in school and with our partner schools to help to deliver adventurous arts projects.
At St Alphege we have demonstrated that:
We continue to embrace every opportunity to advocate for the power of a rich arts and cultural experience for all young people both locally and nationally. We are regularly asked to deliver training, share our outstanding practice or to speak at public events about the impact of our arts offer.
Darren Henley, Chief Executive of Arts Council England stated that: “St Alphege is a shining example of outstanding creative arts provision. You have developed a rich, inspiring, broad and balanced curriculum that offers your pupils the opportunity to explore and build a love of the arts that will remain with them throughout their adult life.”
Head of School: Jacqui Spinks stated that: “The arts is a fundamental part of the curriculum at St Alphege. This is a commitment which is shared by all staff ensuring that all children have access to the highest quality cultural education. Creativity permeates every aspect of our teaching and learning and is reflected in the high standards our children achieve in all subjects at the end of their educational journey with us. We are immensely proud to have achieved this prestigious award which is testament to the outstanding curriculum and ethos at the school.”
Executive Headteacher, Liz Thomas-Friend stated that: “With all the uncertainty and anxiety in society currently, this is a wonderful indication of the promise of youth and that we must ensure that our young children grow up to understand the importance of creativity, self-confidence and community engagement. St Alphege is a beacon of hope and joy in our community.”
Children are naturally creative. It is our job to give them the freedom, materials and space to let their creativity blossom to its full potential.
